subject.title: fix(codex): cap sandbox file copy reads

question: Should Codex sandbox `fs/copy` enforce the same 512 MiB in-memory read cap as `fs/readFile`, or should large copies remain supported through streaming or backend-native copy semantics before merge?
rationale: The patch is a correct memory-safety fix, but it intentionally changes existing large-file copy behavior, so automation should not silently decide the compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Accept the read cap for copy
options.body: Merge the guard knowing files above 512 MiB now fail before app-server buffering, matching the established `fs/readFile` boundary.

options.title: Require streaming copy first
options.body: Hold this PR until the Codex sandbox bridge can copy large files without buffering them through the app-server process.

recommendation.title: Accept the read cap for copy
recommendation.body: Merge the guard knowing files above 512 MiB now fail before app-server buffering, matching the established `fs/readFile` boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: This person merged the PR that introduced the current sandbox exec-server filesystem surface and is the best available routing candidate for accepting the compatibility tradeoff.
